title: Heresies were predicted and serve to test faith
english: The state of the present times also prompts this warning of mine: we should not be astonished at these heresies. We should not be astonished that they exist, for their coming was foretold. Nor should we be astonished that they overturn the faith of some, since they exist for this very purpose: so that faith, by undergoing temptation, might also undergo testing. So it is in vain and without reflection that many people are scandalized by the very fact that heresies have so much power. How much power would they have if they did not exist? When something has been allotted to exist in every way, it receives a cause for which it exists. It gains the force through which it exists, so that it cannot fail to exist.
orientation: Tertullian opens the treatise by telling believers they should not be shocked that heresies exist or that they overturn some people's faith.

title: Heresies have power only over the weak in faith
english: Consider fever, which among the other deadly and torturous ends has been allotted to man for his destruction. We are not astonished that it exists—it does exist—nor that it destroys man, for that is why it exists. In the same way, if we are terrified that heresies, produced for the weakening and destruction of faith, have this power, we should first be terrified that they exist at all. For while they exist, they have power, and while they have power, they exist.

But fever, as an evil, we abhor rather than marvel at, both because of its cause and its power, as is well known; and as far as lies in us, we take precautions against it, since we do not have its abolition in our own power. Heresies, however, bring eternal death and the burning of a greater fire, yet some people prefer to marvel that they have this power rather than to avoid it, even though they have the power to avoid them. But they will have no strength at all if people do not marvel at their strength.

For either while people marvel, heresies are supplied for scandal, or because people are scandalized, they marvel—as if such great power could come from some truth. A fine marvel indeed, that evil should have its own strength! Except that heresies have much power among those who have no power in faith. In a contest of boxers and gladiators, a man does not usually win because he is strong, or because he cannot be beaten, but because the one who was defeated had no strength at all. So that same victor, when later matched against someone in good health, goes away defeated. In just the same way, heresies draw their strength from the weaknesses of certain people, and have no strength at all if they run against a faith in good health.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heresies, like fever, should not be wondered at for their power, because their power comes only from the weakness of those they overcome.

title: The fall of prominent persons does not prove heresy true
english: These weaker people are also in the habit of being built up into ruin by certain persons who have been captured by heresy. Why, they ask, did that man or that woman, people of the greatest faith, the greatest wisdom, the most experienced in the church, go over to the other side? Whoever says this should answer his own question: those whom heresies have been able to change should not be considered wise, or faithful, or experienced at all.

And is it so surprising, I wonder, that someone once approved should later fall away? Saul, good beyond all others, was afterward overturned by envy. David, a good man according to the heart of the Lord, later became guilty of murder and adultery. Solomon, gifted by the Lord with every grace and wisdom, was led into idolatry by women. Only the Son of God was preserved to remain without fault.

What then? If a bishop, if a deacon, if a widow, if a virgin, if a teacher, if even a martyr has slipped from the rule, will heresies on that account seem to possess the truth? Do we test faith by persons, or persons by faith? No one is wise, no one is faithful, no one is great, unless he is a Christian. And no one is a Christian unless he has persevered to the end.

You, being human, know each person only from the outside. You think what you see is what there is. But you see only as far as your eyes reach. Yet the eyes of the Lord, Scripture says, are high. Man looks at the face, but God looks into the heart. And therefore the Lord knows who are his, and he uproots the plant he did not plant, and he shows the first to be last; and he carries a winnowing fork in his hand to cleanse his threshing floor. Let the chaff of light faith fly wherever it will at every blast of temptation; the purer mass of grain will be stored in the Lord's barns.

Did not some of the Lord's own disciples turn away in scandal? Yet the rest did not think they should therefore abandon his footsteps. Those who knew that he was the word of life and had come from God remained in his company to the end, even though he had calmly offered them the chance to leave as well, if they wished.

It is a smaller matter if some abandoned his apostle: Phygelus and Hermogenes, Philetus and Hymenaeus. The betrayer of Christ himself was one of the apostles. Are we surprised when his churches are deserted by certain people, when the things we suffer after the example of Christ himself are what show us to be Christians? They went out from us, Scripture says, but they were not from us. If they had been from us, they would surely have remained with us (1 John 2:19).
orientation: Tertullian is answering the objection that some well-known church members have gone over to heresy, and he argues that their lapse proves nothing about the truth of heresies.

title: Heresies were foretold and serve to test the faithful
english: Let us rather remember both the Lord's pronouncements and the apostolic letters, which announced to us beforehand that heresies would come and prescribed beforehand that they must be avoided. Just as we are not terrified that they exist, so let us not be surprised that they can do the very thing for which they must be avoided.

The Lord teaches that many will come under the skins of sheep as ravenous wolves (Matthew 7:15). What are those sheep skins but the outward surface of the Christian name? What are the ravenous wolves but deceitful minds and spirits, hiding within to attack the flock of Christ? What are the false prophets but false preachers? What are the false apostles but adulterous evangelizers? What are the antichrists, now and always, but rebels against Christ? These are the heresies, attacking the church with the perversity of their doctrines no less than the antichrist will then pursue it with the cruelty of persecution. The difference is this: persecution makes martyrs, while heresy makes only apostates.

And therefore heresies also had to exist, so that whoever are approved might be made manifest, both those who have stood firm in persecutions and those who have not swerved aside into heresies. For it does not avail to understand as approved those who change their faith into heresy. Yet the heretics interpret it otherwise for themselves, because Paul said elsewhere, Examine all things, hold what is good (1 Thessalonians 5:21). As if it were not permitted for those who have examined badly to stumble into the choice of some evil through error.
orientation: Tertullian is addressing believers, urging them to remember that the Lord and the apostles predicted heresies and commanded them to be avoided, so their existence should not cause alarm.

title: Heresies are reproved as a greater evil among divisions
english: Moreover, if Paul rebukes dissensions and schisms, which are without doubt evil, he immediately attaches heresies to them. By joining them to evils, he certainly declares heresies to be an evil, and a greater one at that, since he says he believed about schisms and dissensions because he knew that heresies also had to exist. For Paul shows that at the sight of a more serious evil he readily believed about the lesser ones. Certainly he did not believe about the evils because heresies were good, but rather to warn in advance that there should be no surprise at temptations of a worse kind as well, temptations which, he says, tend to make manifest those who are approved, namely those whom they could not corrupt.

Finally, if the whole passage aims at maintaining unity and restraining separations, and heresies tear people away from unity no less than schisms and dissensions do, then without doubt Paul places heresies in that condition of reproof in which he also places schisms and dissensions. And for this reason he does not make those approved who have turned aside into heresies, since he especially rebukes turning away from such things, teaching all to speak one thing and to think the same thing, which heresies do not allow.
orientation: Tertullian is commenting on Paul's words about divisions and heresies, arguing that Paul counted heresies among evils, not goods.

title: Paul condemns heretics and the Spirit foretold Apelles
english: There is no need to dwell on this further. The same Paul numbers heresies among fleshly crimes when he writes to the Galatians (Galatians 5:19-21), and he advises Titus that a heretical man is to be refused after a first correction, because such a person is perverse and sins, being condemned by himself (Titus 3:10-11). In almost every letter, moreover, he insists that adulterous doctrines are to be fled, and in doing so he censures heresies. The works of heresies are adulterous doctrines. The Greek word "heresies" comes from the meaning of choice, which a person uses either to establish such doctrines or to adopt them. That is why he said the heretic is condemned by himself: because he has chosen for himself the very thing in which he is condemned.

For us, however, nothing from our own judgment is allowed to indulge, nor may we choose what someone has introduced from his own judgment. We have the Lord's apostles as our authors, and they themselves did not choose anything from their own judgment to introduce, but faithfully assigned to the nations the discipline they had received from Christ. Therefore, even if an angel from heaven should evangelize differently, he would be declared anathema by us (Galatians 1:8).

The Holy Spirit had already foreseen that in a certain virgin named Philumene there would come an angel of seduction, transforming himself into an angel of light. Apelles, induced by his signs and tricks, introduced a new heresy.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heresies were already condemned by the apostles, and he now cites Paul's letters and the case of Apelles as proof.

title: Heresies are born from philosophy
english: These are the doctrines of men and demons, born for itching ears from the cleverness of philosophy, which the Lord calls foolishness and chose the foolish things of the world to confound even philosophy itself (1 Corinthians 1:27). For that is the material of philosophy: a presumptuous interpreter of the divine nature and order. The heresies themselves are equipped by philosophy. From there come the aeons and the infinite forms, whatever they are, and the trinity of man in Valentinus; he had been a Platonist. From there comes Marcion's better god, from tranquility; he had come from the Stoics. And when it is said that the soul dies, that is taken from the Epicureans. And when the restoration of the flesh is denied, that is drawn from the single school of all the philosophers. And where matter is made equal with God, that is the teaching of Zeno. And where something about a fiery god is alleged, Heraclitus steps in. The same material is rolled over among heretics and philosophers; the same retracings entangle them: where does evil come from, and why? And where does man come from, and how? And, what Valentinus recently proposed, where does God come from? From enthymesis and ectroma, of course. Wretched Aristotle! He set up dialectic for them, the craftsman of building and destroying, changeable in opinions, forced in conjectures, harsh in arguments, a worker of contentions, troublesome even to himself, retracting everything so that he might treat nothing at all. From there come those fables and endless genealogies, and fruitless questions, and words creeping like cancer, from which the apostle restrains us and testifies by name that philosophy must be avoided, writing to the Colossians: See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to human tradition, apart from the providence of the Holy Spirit (Colossians 2:8). He had been at Athens, and he knew that human wisdom, the imitator and corrupter of truth, from his encounters there, was itself divided into its own heresies by the variety of mutually opposing schools. What then does Athens have to do with Jerusalem? What does the academy have to do with the church? What do heretics have to do with Christians? Our instruction is from the porch of Solomon, who himself had handed down that the Lord must be sought in simplicity of heart. Let those who have produced a Stoic and Platonic and dialectic Christianity see to it. We have no need of curiosity after Jesus Christ, nor of inquiry after the gospel. When we believe, we desire nothing beyond belief. For this we believe first: that there is nothing further that we ought to believe.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretical teachings derive from pagan philosophy, not from the apostolic tradition.

title: The command to seek was for the Jews before Christ was known
english: So I come to that point which our own people put forward as an excuse for curiosity, and which heretics press upon us to force scrupulosity upon us. They say, “Seek, and you will find” (Matthew 7:7). Let us remember when the Lord uttered this saying. I think it was at the very first beginnings of his teaching, when everyone was still doubting whether he was the Christ, when Peter had not yet declared him to be the Son of God, and when even John had ceased to be certain about him. Rightly, then, was it said at that time, “Seek, and you will find,” when the one who was not yet known still had to be sought.

And this was as far as the Jews were concerned. For the whole force of that reproof belongs to them, since they had somewhere to seek Christ. “They have,” he says, “Moses and Elijah”—that is, the law and the prophets proclaiming Christ—just as he says openly elsewhere: “Search the Scriptures, in which you hope for salvation; for they speak of me” (John 5:39). This is what “Seek, and you will find” means. For it is clear that what follows also applies to the Jews: “Knock, and it will be opened to you” (Matthew 7:7). The Jews had formerly been near God; afterwards, cast out for their offenses, they began to be outside God. The Gentiles, however, were never near God—only a drop from a bucket and dust from a threshing floor, and always outside. So how will the one who was always outside knock at a place where he never was? What door does he know, into which he was never received nor ever cast out? Is it not rather the one who knows he was once inside and has been driven out who knocked, and who knows the door?

Likewise, “Ask, and you will receive” (Matthew 7:7) belongs to the one who knew from whom he should ask, and from whom something had been promised—namely, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, whom the Gentiles knew no more than they knew any of his promises. And that is why he was speaking to Israel: “I was not sent,” he says, “except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel” (Matthew 15:24). He had not yet thrown the children’s bread to the dogs; he had not yet commanded them to go into the way of the Gentiles. Only at the end did he command them to go and teach and baptize the Gentiles, soon to receive the Holy Spirit, who would lead them into all truth (Matthew 28:19; John 16:13). And this, too, he does for that purpose.

But if the apostles were appointed as teachers for the Gentiles, and they themselves were also about to receive the Holy Spirit as their teacher, then far less did “Seek, and you will find” apply to us, since teaching was to come to us unsought through the apostles, and to the apostles themselves through the Holy Spirit. All the Lord’s sayings, indeed, are set before all people; through the ears of the Jews they have passed down to us. But most of them were directed at particular persons and have established for us not the force of a command but an example.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the gospel command 'Seek and you will find' was addressed to the Jews before they recognized Christ, not to Christians who already believe.

title: The limit of seeking: believe what Christ instituted, then seek nothing further
english: Now let me step down from that position of my own accord. Let it be said to everyone, “Seek and you will find” (Matthew 7:7); yet even here the meaning demands to be settled by the helm of interpretation. No divine utterance is so loose and scattered that only the words are defended and the reason of the words is not established. But first of all I lay this down: that one definite and certain thing was instituted by Christ which the nations must believe in every way, and that they must seek for this reason, so that when they have found it they may believe. Moreover, there cannot be an endless inquiry into one definite and certain institution. You must seek until you find, and believe when you have found, and nothing more, except to guard what you have believed—while you believe this further, that nothing else is to be believed, and therefore nothing else is to be sought again, once you have found and believed what was instituted by him who commands you to seek nothing other than what he instituted. If anyone doubts about this, it will be established that what was instituted by Christ is with us. In the meantime, out of confidence in the proof, I go ahead and warn certain people that nothing is to be sought beyond what they have believed—that this is what they ought to have sought—lest they interpret “Seek and you will find” without the discipline of reason.
orientation: Tertullian is beginning his argument that the command 'Seek and you will find' has a fixed limit, namely the doctrine Christ instituted, which once found and believed leaves nothing further to seek.

title: The limits of seeking: what, when, and how far
english: The reasoning behind this saying rests on three points: the thing, the time, and the manner. The thing, so that you consider what is to be sought; the time, when; the manner, how far. What is to be sought, then, is what Christ instituted—as long, of course, as you have not found it, and until you do find it. You have found it when you have believed. For you would not have believed if you had not found it, just as you would not have sought unless you intended to find. So you sought in order to find, and you found in order to believe. By believing, you have brought the whole extension of seeking and finding to a fixed end. The very fruit of seeking has set this limit for you. The one who does not want you to believe anything other than what he instituted—and therefore does not want you to seek anything else—has dug this boundary for you. Otherwise, if because so many other things have been instituted by others we must keep seeking as long as we can keep finding, then we will always be seeking and never actually believe. Where will the end of seeking be? Where the stopping-point of believing? Where the completion of finding? With Marcion? But Valentinus also proposes, “Seek and you will find” (Matthew 7:7). With Valentinus? But Apelles will knock at me with this pronouncement too, and Ebion and Simon and all the rest in turn have nothing else by which they insinuate themselves to me and bind me to themselves. So I will be nowhere, while everywhere I am met with “Seek and you will find”—and as if I were nowhere, as if I had never grasped what Christ instituted, what ought to be sought, what must be believed.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the command 'Seek and you will find' has fixed limits, and that once a person has believed what Christ instituted, seeking must stop.

title: Seeking only belongs to those who lack or lost
english: Error goes unpunished only if no offense is committed—though to err is itself an offense. I say it again: the person who abandons nothing wanders without penalty. But if I believed what I ought to have believed, and then decide something else must be sought again, I am certainly hoping that something else will be found. I would never hope for that unless I had either not believed when I seemed to believe, or had stopped believing. So by abandoning my faith, I am found to be a denier. Let me say it once for all: no one seeks except the one who either never had or has lost.

That old woman had lost one of her ten coins, and that is why she was searching; but once she found it, she stopped searching. The neighbor had no bread, and that is why he was knocking; but once the door was opened and he received it, he stopped knocking. The widow was asking the judge to hear her because she was not being admitted; but once she was heard, she pressed no further. So there is an end to seeking, to knocking, and to asking. For it says, "To the one who asks it will be given, and to the one who knocks it will be opened, and to the one who seeks it will be found" (Matthew 7:7).

Let the one who always seeks look to it, because he does not find. He is seeking where nothing will be found. Let the one who always knocks look to it, because it will never be opened. He is knocking where no one is. Let the one who always asks look to it, because he will never be heard. He is asking from one who does not hear.
orientation: Tertullian is answering the heretics' use of 'Seek and you will find' by arguing that seeking is only for those who do not yet have or have lost what they seek.

title: Where seeking is still permitted
english: Even if we must still seek, and always seek, where should the seeking happen? Among heretics, where everything is foreign and hostile to our truth, and where we are forbidden to go? What servant hopes to get food from a stranger—not to say from his own master's enemy? What soldier seeks a gift and pay from those not bound by treaty—not to say from enemy kings—unless he is plainly a deserter, a turncoat, and a rebel? Even that old woman was searching for her drachma inside her own house; even that man was knocking at his neighbor's door; even that widow was pleading with a judge who was not her enemy, though he was harsh. No one can be built up from the place where he is destroyed; no one is enlightened by the one who darkens him. So let us seek in our own, from our own, and about our own—and only what can come into question with the rule of faith safe.
orientation: Tertullian has just shown that the command to seek was for those who had not yet found; now he asks where any remaining seeking may rightly be done.

title: The Rule of Faith Stated
english: The rule of faith—so that from this point I declare what we defend—is that by which we believe there is one God alone, and no other besides the creator of the world, who produced all things from nothing through his word sent down first of all. This word, called his Son, was seen in the name of God in various ways by the patriarchs, was always heard in the prophets, and was finally brought down by the Spirit and power of God the Father into the virgin Mary, became flesh in her womb, and was born from her as Jesus Christ. From then on he preached the new law and the new promise of the kingdom of heaven, performed miracles, was crucified, rose on the third day, was taken up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of the Father. He sent the vicarious power of the Holy Spirit to lead believers, and he will come with glory to take up the saints into the fruit of eternal life and the heavenly promises, and to judge the profane with perpetual fire, after the resurrection of both groups has taken place with the restoration of the flesh. This rule, instituted by Christ, as will be proved, has no questions among us except those which heresies introduce and which make heretics.
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by stating the rule of faith, the fixed summary of Christian belief, which he will defend against heretics.

title: Faith, not curiosity, is the rule; heretics who still seek are not Christians
english: But as long as the form of the rule remains in its proper order, you may seek and discuss as much as you like and pour out all the desire of your curiosity, if anything seems to you to hang in ambiguity or be shadowed by obscurity. There is certainly some brother endowed with the gift of knowledge, some one among the trained, some curious person who has spent time with you—yet one who seeks with you. In the end he will know better that you should be ignorant, so that you may not know what you ought not to know, because you know what you ought to know. "Your faith," he says, "has saved you," not your exercise in the Scriptures. Faith is placed in the rule; it has law and salvation from observing the law. Exercise, however, consists in curiosity, having glory only from the pursuit of skill. Let curiosity yield to faith; let glory yield to salvation. Certainly let them either not clamor against it, or be quiet. To know nothing against the rule is to know everything.

Even if heretics were not enemies of the truth, even if we were not warned beforehand to avoid them, what sort of thing is it to confer with people who themselves still profess to be seeking? For if they are still truly seeking, they have found nothing certain yet, and therefore whatever they seem to hold for the time being, they show their doubt as long as they seek. And so you, who likewise seek, looking to those who themselves seek, doubtful toward the doubtful, uncertain toward the uncertain, blind led by the blind, you must necessarily be led into the pit. But since they pretend to still be seeking for the sake of deceiving us, so that by injecting anxiety they may insinuate their arguments into us—indeed, when they come to us, they immediately defend the very things they said needed to be sought—we must refute them in such a way that they know we are deniers not of Christ, but of themselves. For when they are still seeking, they do not yet hold; and when they do not hold, they have not yet believed; and when they have not yet believed, they are not Christians. But when they do hold and believe, they nevertheless say that seeking is necessary, in order to defend. Before they defend, they deny what they confess—that they have not yet believed, while they seek. Therefore those who are not Christians even to themselves, how much more are they not Christians to us? By what faith do they dispute, who come through deceit? What truth do they plead for, who introduce it from falsehood? But they themselves argue from the Scriptures, and from the Scriptures they persuade! From where else, of course, could they speak about matters of faith, except from the writings of faith?
orientation: Tertullian has just stated the rule of faith and now argues that once the rule is held, there is nothing further to seek, and that heretics who claim still to be seeking thereby show they are not Christians.

title: Heretics must be barred from arguing over the Scriptures
english: So we have come to the purpose. This is what we were directing our course toward, and what we were building up beforehand with the preface of our address: that from this point we may engage the matter on which our adversaries challenge us. They put forward the Scriptures, and by this boldness of theirs they immediately disturb some people. In the actual encounter, they weary the strong, capture the weak, and send away those in between with lingering unease. This step, then, above all, we block: they are not to be admitted to any dispute over the Scriptures. If these are their strength, so that they may possess them, it must be examined to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs, so that no one may be admitted to them to whom it in no way belongs.
orientation: Tertullian is now moving to the main point of his treatise: heretics use the Scriptures to argue, but they must not be allowed to do so because the Scriptures do not belong to them.

title: Why heretics must not be given a debate over Scripture
english: I would not have introduced this from a plan of distrust, or from a desire of entering upon the arrangement otherwise, unless that principle stood first: our faith owes obedience to the apostle, who forbids entering into questions, giving ears to new words, and meeting with a heretic after one correction, not after a disputation. So thoroughly has he forbidden disputation that he designates correction as the reason for meeting with a heretic, and this once only, because he is not a Christian, lest he seem to be chastised in the manner of a Christian, once and again and under two or three witnesses, since he is to be chastised for this very reason: that there should be no disputing with him. And then, because a contest over the Scriptures profits nothing, except plainly that it may enter upon the overturning of the stomach or of the brain.
orientation: Tertullian is explaining why he has decided to refuse heretics any dispute over the Scriptures, grounding this refusal in the apostle Paul's command.

title: Heretics corrupt the Scriptures and make debate futile
english: This heresy does not accept certain Scriptures, and the ones it does accept it overturns with additions and subtractions to suit the arrangement of its own teaching. Even when it accepts them, it does not accept them whole, and if it presents them as whole in some measure, it still twists them by inventing different expositions. The adulterating sense obstructs the truth just as much as the corrupting pen. Empty presumptions necessarily refuse to recognize the very things by which they are refuted. They rely on what they have fabricated from falsehood and what they have seized from ambiguity. What will you gain, you who are most practiced in the Scriptures, when whatever you defend is denied from the other side, and whatever you deny is defended? You will lose nothing but your voice in the dispute, and you will gain nothing but bile from the blaspheming.
orientation: Tertullian is describing how heretics handle the Scriptures, and then addressing a hypothetical defender of the faith who tries to argue with them from Scripture.

title: The skeptic leaves more uncertain after debate
english: But the person for whose sake you enter a contest over the Scriptures, to steady him when he wavers—will he turn toward the truth, or rather toward heresies? Moved by the very fact that he sees you have made no progress, with the opposing side equal in denying and defending, with the standing certainly equal, the dispute will depart more uncertain, not knowing which heresy to judge. These things, of course, they can also turn back against us. For they too must say that it is rather we who introduce adulterations of the Scriptures and falsehoods of expositions, since they likewise claim the truth for themselves.
orientation: Tertullian is addressing a Christian who would debate heretics from Scripture, and now asks what happens to the doubting person for whose sake the debate is entered.

title: The contest must first be over who owns the faith
english: So there must be no appeal to the Scriptures, and no contest established in them where victory is either nonexistent, or uncertain, or not certain enough. For even if a comparison of the Scriptures did not turn out in such a way as to make both sides stand equal, the order of things was requiring that this be proposed first, which alone is now to be disputed: to whom the faith itself belongs, whose the Scriptures are, from whom, and through whom, and when, and to whom was handed down the discipline by which people become Christians. For where it has appeared that the truth of the Christian discipline and faith is, there will be the truth of the Scriptures and of their interpretations and of all Christian traditions.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretics have no right to debate Scripture, because the prior question is who the Scriptures and the faith belong to.

title: The apostolic origin and unity of the churches
english: May Christ Jesus our Lord permit me to say this for the moment, whoever he is, of whatever god he is the son, of whatever substance he is man and God, of whatever faith he is the teacher, of whatever reward he is the promiser: what he was, what he had been, what will of the Father he was carrying out, what he determined man should do, he himself was declaring all this while he lived on earth, whether openly to the people or privately to his disciples, from whom he had chosen twelve chief men to be at his side, destined as teachers for the nations.

And so when one of them was struck off, he ordered the remaining eleven, as he was departing to the Father after his resurrection, to go and teach the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).

Immediately, then, the apostles, a name that means sent ones, took Matthias by lot as the twelfth in place of Judas, according to the authority of the prophecy in the psalm of David (Acts 1:26; Psalm 109:8), and having obtained the promised power of the Holy Spirit for miracles and speech (Acts 2:4), they first testified to faith in Jesus Christ throughout Judea and established churches, and then went out into the world and proclaimed the same teaching of the same faith to the nations.

In the same way they founded churches in each city, from which the other churches afterward borrowed the shoot of faith and the seeds of teaching, and still borrow them daily, so that they become churches.
And for this reason they too will be counted as apostolic, as offspring of apostolic churches.
Every kind of thing must be judged by its origin.
And so all those churches, many and great as they are, are that one first church from the apostles, from which all the rest come.

Thus all are first and all are apostolic, while all together prove their unity by the communion of peace, the name of brotherhood, and the exchange of hospitality, rights which no other principle governs than the one tradition of the same sacred mystery.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the true faith and the Scriptures belong to the apostolic churches, and here he traces how Christ's teaching was handed down through the apostles to the churches they founded.

title: The Rule for Testing Doctrine by Apostolic Churches
english: From this point, then, I direct my legal objection. If the Lord Jesus Christ sent the apostles to preach, no other preachers are to be received than those whom Christ appointed. For no one knows the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son has revealed him (Matthew 11:27). And the Son does not appear to have revealed him to any others than the apostles whom he sent to preach, preaching, of course, what he had revealed to them.

And what they preached, that is, what Christ revealed to them, should be proved, I will also maintain here, in no other way than through those same churches which the apostles themselves founded. They founded them by preaching to them both with the living voice, as they say, and afterward through letters.

If this is so, it is settled that every doctrine which agrees with those apostolic churches, the mothers and originals of the faith, is to be assigned to the truth. Such a doctrine undoubtedly holds what the churches received from the apostles, the apostles from Christ, and Christ from God. But every doctrine that savors against the truth of the churches and of the apostles of Christ and of God is to be judged beforehand as coming from falsehood.

It remains, then, for me to demonstrate whether this doctrine of ours, whose rule of faith I set out above, is counted as coming from the tradition of the apostles, and from this very fact whether the others come from falsehood. We share communion with the apostolic churches, because no doctrine of ours is different. This is the testimony of the truth.
orientation: Tertullian is laying down the legal objection that only the churches founded by the apostles can prove what Christ revealed to them.

title: The apostles knew all truth and passed it on
english: But the proof is so easy that if it were brought forward at once, nothing would remain to be reconsidered. let us, as if it had not been brought forward by us, give room for the moment to the opposing side, in case they think they can raise anything to weaken this legal objection. They are in the habit of saying that the apostles did not know everything. They are driven by the same madness with which they turn things back again and say that the apostles did know everything, but did not hand on everything to everyone. In both cases they cast blame on Christ, who sent apostles either too poorly instructed or too little straightforward.

Who, then, of sound mind can believe that those men were ignorant of anything? The Lord gave them as teachers, keeping them inseparable in his company, in his discipleship, in his daily life. To them he explained every obscure matter privately, saying to them that it was given to them to know hidden things which the people were not permitted to understand. Did anything escape Peter, who was called the rock of the church to be built, who obtained the keys of the kingdom of heaven and the power of loosing and binding in heaven and on earth? Did anything escape John, the Lord's most beloved, leaning on his breast, to whom alone the Lord pointed out Judas the betrayer beforehand, whom he entrusted to Mary as a son in his own place? What did he want them to be ignorant of, those to whom he also showed his glory and Moses and Elijah, and above all the Father's voice from heaven? Not as if he rejected the others, but because every word will stand on three witnesses.

So they were ignorant, were they, those for whom after the resurrection too he deigned to explain all the Scriptures on the road? He had indeed said at one time, 'I have many things still to say to you, but you cannot bear them now,' yet he added, 'When that spirit of truth comes, he himself will lead you into all truth.' He showed that they were ignorant of nothing, since he had promised that they would attain all truth through the spirit of truth. And he certainly fulfilled his promise, as the Acts of the Apostles prove by the descent of the Holy Spirit.

Those who do not receive this writing cannot be of the Holy Spirit either, since they cannot yet recognize that the Holy Spirit was sent to the disciples. Nor should they claim to defend the church, since they have no way to prove when and with what beginnings this body was established. For it matters that much to them not to have proofs for the things they defend, lest the exposure of their lies be admitted along with them.
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who claim the apostles either did not know everything or did not hand on everything, in order to weaken his legal objection that heretics have no right to the Scriptures.

title: Paul's rebuke of Peter proves no new gospel
english: So to insult some ignorance in the apostles, they bring up the fact that Peter and those with him were rebuked by Paul. "You see," they say, "something was lacking in them." From this they then build the claim that a fuller knowledge could have arrived later, the kind that came to Paul when he rebuked his predecessors. Here too I can say to those who reject the Acts of the Apostles: first you must show who this Paul was, what he was before he became an apostle, and how he became an apostle, since they make heavy use of him in other questions as well. For even if he declares himself an apostle, once a persecutor, that is not enough for anyone who believes with examination, since not even the Lord himself bore witness about himself. But they believe without the Scriptures, so that they believe against the Scriptures. Still, let them prove from what they allege—that Peter was rebuked by Paul—that another form of the gospel was introduced by Paul beyond the one Peter and the rest had delivered before him.

But in fact, changed from a persecutor into a preacher, he is brought to the brothers by the brothers, as one of the brothers, and to those by those who had put on the faith from the apostles. Then, as he himself relates, he went up to Jerusalem to know Peter, from the duty and right, of course, of the same faith and preaching. For they would not have marveled that a persecutor had become a preacher if he were preaching something contrary, nor would they have glorified the Lord because his adversary Paul had come to them. So they gave him the right hand, a sign of concord and agreement, and arranged among themselves a distribution of the work, not a separation of the gospel—not so that one would preach one thing and the other another, but so that one would preach to one group and the other to another: Peter to the circumcision, Paul to the Gentiles.

For the rest, if Peter was rebuked because, after living together with Gentiles, he later separated himself from their company out of respect for persons, that was certainly a fault of conduct, not of preaching. For it was not because of this that another god than the Creator was being announced, or another Christ than the one from Mary, or another hope than the resurrection.
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who use Paul's rebuke of Peter to claim that the apostles lacked full knowledge and that Paul later brought a fuller gospel.

title: Paul's accommodation does not prove a hidden doctrine
english: I have no desire—indeed, it is far from my intent—to set the apostles against one another. But since those most perverse people put forward that rebuke as a pretext to make the earlier teaching suspect, I will answer as if for Peter: Paul himself said that he had become all things to all people, a Jew to Jews and a non-Jew to non-Jews, so that he might win over everyone (1 Corinthians 9:20-22). So they found fault with certain things according to the times, the persons, and the circumstances, and they themselves equally committed those same things according to the times, the persons, and the circumstances—just as if Peter had rebuked Paul because, while forbidding circumcision, Paul himself circumcised Timothy (Acts 16:3). Let those who judge the apostles see to it. It is well that Peter is made equal to Paul even in martyrdom. But even if Paul was caught up to the third heaven and carried into paradise and heard certain things there, those things cannot be thought to have been such as would make him more fully instructed for another doctrine, since their condition was such that they were not to be disclosed to any human being (2 Corinthians 12:2-4). But if something of that kind leaked out to someone's knowledge, and some heresy claims to follow it, then either Paul is guilty of betraying a secret, or someone else must be shown to have been caught up into paradise afterward, to whom it was permitted to speak aloud what Paul was not allowed to whisper.
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who use Peter's rebuke to make the earlier apostolic teaching suspect, and he now defends Paul's conduct and the public nature of apostolic doctrine.

title: The deposit was not a secret doctrine
english: But as we have said, it is the same madness when they admit that they have ignored nothing concerning the apostles and did not preach different things among themselves, yet they refuse to believe that the apostles revealed everything to everyone. They claim that some things were entrusted openly and to all, while others were entrusted secretly and to a few, because Paul also used this word to Timothy: "O Timothy, guard the deposit" (1 Timothy 6:20), and again, "Keep the good deposit" (2 Timothy 1:14). What is this deposit, so silent that it is reckoned as another doctrine? Or is it that charge of which he says, "I commend this charge to you, my child Timothy" (1 Timothy 1:18)? Or that command of which he says, "I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and Jesus Christ, who bore witness before Pontius Pilate to the good confession, to keep the command" (1 Timothy 6:13)? But what command and what charge? From what is written above and below it will be understood that nothing is being hinted at in this saying about some more hidden doctrine, but rather that he is insisting that no other doctrine be admitted besides the one Timothy had heard from him—and I think openly. "Before many witnesses," he says (2 Timothy 2:2). If they do not want the church to be understood by these many witnesses, it makes no difference, since nothing was silent that was brought forth before many witnesses. Nor is the fact that he wanted Timothy to entrust these things to faithful men who would be able to teach others also to be interpreted as an argument for some hidden gospel. For when he says "these things," he is speaking about the things he was writing about at that moment. About hidden things, as about absent things, he would have said "those things," not "these things," in his own conscience.
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who claim the apostles taught some things openly and some things secretly, and he is examining Paul's words to Timothy about the deposit.

title: The apostles preached openly, not in secret
english: It followed, then, that when he entrusted the administration of the gospel to someone, since it was not to be administered carelessly or at random, he added, in keeping with the Lord's own words, that he should not throw a pearl to pigs or a holy thing to dogs (Matthew 7:6). The Lord said this openly, without any hint of some hidden mystery. He himself had commanded that whatever they heard in darkness and in secret they should proclaim in the light and on the housetops (Matthew 10:27). He himself had prefigured through a parable that they should not keep a single mina, that is, a single word of his, stored away in hiding without fruit (Luke 19:20). He himself taught that a lamp is not usually hidden under a bushel, but placed on a lampstand so that it gives light to everyone in the house (Matthew 5:15).

The apostles either neglected these instructions or understood them very poorly, if they failed to carry them out by hiding something of the Light, that is, of the word of God and the mystery of Christ. They feared no one, as far as I know: not the violence of the Jews, not that of the Gentiles. All the more, then, they surely preached freely in the church, since they did not keep silent in synagogues and public places. Indeed, they could not have converted Jews or brought in Gentiles unless they set forth in an orderly way what they wanted them to believe. Much less would they have withheld anything from churches that already believed, to entrust it separately to a few others.

And yet, even if they did discuss certain matters among the household, so to speak, it must not be believed that these were things that would introduce another rule of faith, different from and contrary to the one they proclaimed publicly in the catholic manner. As if they declared one God in the church and another in private lodging, presented one substance of Christ in the open and another in secret, announced one hope of resurrection to everyone and another to a few. For they themselves pleaded in their letters that everyone should speak the same thing and one thing, and that there should be no schisms and dissensions in the church, because whether Paul or the others, they preached the same things (1 Corinthians 1:10). Otherwise they would have remembered: "Let your speech be: yes, yes, no, no; for anything more than this is from evil" (Matthew 5:37), so that they would not handle the gospel in divergent ways.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the apostles did not keep any hidden doctrine back from the churches, since the Lord commanded open proclamation.

title: The heretics' objection from corrected churches
english: If, then, it is unbelievable either that the apostles did not know the fullness of the preaching or that they did not publish the whole order of the rule to everyone, let us consider whether perhaps the apostles did teach simply and fully, but the churches through their own fault received differently from what the apostles were bringing forth. You will find all these incitements of scrupulosity put forward by the heretics. They hold up the churches rebuked by the apostle: "O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you?" (Galatians 3:1), and "You were running so well; who hindered you?" (Galatians 5:7), and the very beginning: "I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from him who called you in grace to another gospel" (Galatians 1:6). Likewise it was written to the Corinthians that they were still carnal, fed on milk and not yet ready for solid food (1 Corinthians 3:1-2), who thought they knew something when they did not yet know how they ought to know (1 Corinthians 8:2). When they set the rebuked churches before us, let them believe those churches were corrected. But let them also recognize the churches over whose faith and knowledge and conduct the apostle rejoices and gives thanks to God—churches which even today share the rights of one institution with those rebuked ones.
orientation: Tertullian is answering the heretics' claim that the apostles did not teach the full rule of faith to all churches, and now he turns to the heretics' use of Paul's rebukes to certain churches.

title: The impossibility that all the churches erred
english: Come now, suppose they all went astray; suppose the apostle was deceived in bearing witness; suppose the Holy Spirit looked upon no church so as to lead it into truth, though Christ sent him for this purpose and asked the Father for him so that he might be the teacher of truth; suppose the steward of God's household, the vicar of Christ, neglected his duty by allowing the churches to understand one thing and believe another than what he himself was preaching through the apostles—is it really likely that so many and such great churches erred into one faith? Among many people, no single outcome is the same. The error of the churches' teaching should have produced different results. But what is found as one thing among many is not an error; it is tradition. So let anyone dare to say that those who handed it down went astray.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the apostolic churches cannot all have fallen into error, since their shared faith must be tradition, not mistake.

title: Error reigned until heresies came
english: However the error came about, error certainly reigned as long as there were no heresies. Truth was waiting to set free some Marcionites and Valentinians. In the meantime the gospel was preached wrongly, faith was believed wrongly; so many thousands upon thousands were wrongly baptized, so many works of faith were wrongly performed, so many miracles, so many gifts of grace were wrongly worked, so many priesthoods, so many ministries were wrongly fulfilled, so many martyrdoms were wrongly crowned. Or if not wrongly and not in vain, what kind of thing is it that the things of God ran ahead before it was known whose God they were? Christians before Christ was found? Heresies before true doctrine? But in all things truth precedes the image; the likeness follows after. Otherwise it is quite absurd that heresy should be taken for the earlier doctrine, especially since it is the true doctrine itself that foretold that future heresies must be guarded against. It was written to the church of that doctrine—indeed, the doctrine itself writes to the church: "Even if an angel from heaven should preach a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let him be anathema" (Galatians 1:8).
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that if the apostolic doctrine had been wrong, error would have reigned unchecked until the heretics appeared, which is absurd.

title: Marcion and Valentinus as late innovators
english: Where then was Marcion, the shipmaster from Pontus, the student of Stoicism? Where then was Valentinus, the follower of the Platonic school? For it is agreed that they were not so very long ago—roughly in the reign of Antoninus—and that they first believed in the doctrine of the catholic church at Rome under the blessed bishop Eleutherus, until their restless curiosity, by which they were also corrupting the brothers, got them expelled once and then again. Marcion, indeed, was expelled with the two hundred thousand sesterces he had brought into the church, and at last they were banished into permanent separation and scattered the poisons of their doctrines. Afterwards Marcion confessed repentance and accepted the condition offered him—that he would receive peace if he restored to the church the others he had trained for destruction—but he was overtaken by death. For heresies had to exist. Yet heresies are not good just because they had to exist. As if evil did not also have to exist. For the Lord also had to be betrayed, but woe to the betrayer—so let no one defend heresies even from this. If the pedigree of Apelles must also be examined, he is no more ancient than Marcion, his founder and shaper. But falling into sin with a woman, he deserted Marcion's discipline of continence and withdrew from the eyes of his most holy teacher to Alexandria. Returning after some years, he was no better—except that he was no longer a Marcionite—and he crashed into another woman, that virgin Philumene whom we mentioned above, later herself a notorious prostitute. Overcome by her spiritual activity, he wrote the Phaneroseis based on what he learned from her. Even now there are people still alive in the world who remember them—their own disciples and successors—so that later generations cannot deny it. And indeed they are refuted by their own works, as the Lord said. For if Marcion separated the New Testament from the Old, he is later than what he separated, because he could not separate what had not been united. What was united before it was later separated shows that the separator came after. Likewise Valentinus, by expounding differently and no doubt correcting—by that very name, whatever he corrects he shows to have been faulty before and to have belonged to someone else. These are the ones we name as the more notable and frequent adulterers of the truth. But there is also some Nigidius or other, and Hermogenes, and many others still walking about perverting the ways of the Lord. Let them show me from what authority they have come forth. If they preach another god, how do they use the things, writings, and names of that God against whom they preach? If the same God, how do they do it differently? Let them prove they are new apostles: let them say Christ has come down again, taught again himself, been crucified again, died again, risen again. For that is how the apostle described it; that is how he is accustomed to make apostles—and to give them the power to produce the same signs he himself produced. I want their powers to be brought forward too—except that I recognize their greatest power, by which they rival the apostles in a perverse way. For the apostles made the living from the dead; these make the dead from the living.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretics are later than the apostolic truth, and here he traces the careers of Marcion, Valentinus, and Apelles to show they are recent innovators.

title: The parable of wheat and weeds proves truth is prior, falsehood later
english: But let me turn back from that digression to argue for the priority of truth and the lateness of falsehood, drawing support as well from that parable in which the good seed of wheat is sown first by the Lord, and afterwards the enemy, the devil, lets in the adulteration of barren wild oats and hay. For this properly pictures the distinction between doctrines, since elsewhere too the word of God is compared to seed (Luke 8:11). So the very order of things makes it clear that what was handed down first is the Lord's and is true, while what was let in later is foreign and false. That verdict will stand against every later heresy, none of which has any constancy from conscience to claim the truth for itself.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretical teachings are later than the apostolic truth, and he now turns to the parable of the wheat and the weeds as evidence.

title: Apostolic succession as the test of true churches
english: But suppose some of them dare to insert themselves into the apostolic age, so that they may seem to have been handed down by the apostles because they existed under the apostles. We can say to them: Let them produce the origins of their churches. Let them unroll the order of their bishops, running down from the beginning by succession in such a way that their first bishop had as his author and predecessor one of the apostles or apostolic men who nevertheless persevered with the apostles.

For this is how the apostolic churches present their records. The church of Smyrna reports that Polycarp was placed there by John. The church of Rome reports that Clement was ordained by Peter in the same way. Likewise the other churches certainly exhibit those whom they have as transmitters of the apostolic seed, appointed to the episcopate by the apostles.

Let the heretics invent something of this kind. For what is forbidden to them after blasphemy? But even if they invent it, they will gain nothing. For their doctrine itself, when compared with the apostolic doctrine, will declare by its diversity and contrariety that it has neither any apostle nor any apostolic man as its author. Just as the apostles would not have taught things different from one another, so apostolic men would not have published things contrary to the apostles—unless those who learned from the apostles preached otherwise.

By this standard, then, they will be tested by those churches which, although they can produce no apostle or apostolic man as their author, being much later and indeed being established daily, nevertheless are counted as no less apostolic because of the kinship of doctrine, since they agree in the same faith.

So all heresies, challenged by our churches according to both standards, must prove themselves apostolic in whatever way they think they are. But they are so far from being apostolic, and so unable to prove what they are not, that they are not received into peace and communion by churches that are apostolic in any way—clearly because of the diversity of their mystery, they are in no way apostolic.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretics cannot claim apostolic origin, and now proposes that any church claiming apostolic descent must produce the succession of its bishops from an apostle or apostolic man.

title: The apostles already marked and condemned the doctrines now held by heretics
english: I add to this a review of the very doctrines that existed under the apostles, which were both demonstrated and condemned by those same apostles. For in this way they will be more easily refuted, since they are either caught as having existed already then, or as having taken seeds from those things that already existed then.

Paul notes in his first letter to the Corinthians those who deny and doubt the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:12). This opinion belonged to the Sadducees. Marcion, Apelles, and Valentinus seize a part of it, and any others who weaken the resurrection of the flesh.
And writing to the Galatians, he inveighs against those who observe and defend circumcision and the law (Galatians 5:2-4). This is the heresy of Ebion.
Instructing Timothy, he also rebukes those who forbid marriage (1 Timothy 4:3). Marcion and Apelles, his follower, teach this.
He likewise touches those who said the resurrection had already happened (2 Timothy 2:18). The Valentinians assert this about themselves.

But when he names endless genealogies (1 Timothy 1:4), Valentinus is recognized. Among his followers, that Aeon—some new one with more than one name—generates from his own Grace, Sense and Truth; and these in turn produce from themselves Word and Life; and then these generate Man and Church, from which first group of eight Aeons ten others arise, and then the remaining twelve Aeons with astonishing names, into a mere fable of thirty Aeons.

The same apostle, when he disapproves of those serving the elements (Colossians 2:20), points to something of Hermogenes, who introduces uncreated matter and compares it to the uncreated God, and so makes the mother of the elements a goddess and can serve her whom he compares to God.
John, in the Revelation, is ordered to chastise those eating things sacrificed to idols and committing fornication (Revelation 2:14). There are now other Nicolaitans. It is called the Gaian heresy.

But in his epistle he calls those especially antichrists who deny that Christ has come in the flesh, and who do not think Jesus is the Son of God (1 John 4:3). Marcion claimed the former, Ebion the latter.
The discipline of Simonian magic, serving angels, was itself also counted among idolatries and was condemned by the apostle Peter in the person of Simon himself.
orientation: Tertullian is showing that the doctrines of present-day heretics were already known and condemned by the apostles in their own time.

title: Heresies under the apostles and the late revelation of false gods
english: These are, I think, the kinds of adulterous doctrines which we learn from the apostles themselves existed in their own time. And yet among so many varieties of perversity we find no teaching that raised a controversy about the God creator of all things. No one dared to suspect another god. There was more hesitation about the Son than about the Father, until Marcion introduced another god of goodness alone besides the creator, and Apelles made the creator some glorious angel of the higher god, I do not know which, the god of the law and of Israel, affirming him to be fiery, and Valentinus scattered his own aeons and derived the origin of the creator god from the defect of one aeon. To these alone, and to these first, was the truth of divinity revealed—they obtained, of course, a greater favor and a fuller grace from the devil, who wished to rival God in this way too: from the teachings of poisons he would make disciples above their master, something the Lord denied (Matthew 10:24). Let all heresies choose for themselves the times when they existed, since it does not matter which time, as long as they are not from the truth; and certainly those which were not under the apostles could not have existed then. If they had existed, they would also have been named, so that they too might have been checked. Those which did exist under the apostles are condemned in their very naming. Therefore, whether the same ones are now somewhat more polished which were crude under the apostles, they have their condemnation from that fact; or whether some were different, and others arose afterward and usurped certain opinions from them, by sharing in their preaching they must necessarily share also in their condemnation, since that principle of lateness mentioned above precedes them—even if they shared nothing of the condemned doctrines, they would be judged by their age alone, all the more adulterous because they were not even named by the apostles. From this it is established more firmly that these are the ones which were even then being announced as still to come.
orientation: Tertullian is surveying the heretical doctrines that existed in apostolic times and arguing that the major heresies about the creator God arose only later.

title: The challenge to heretics to prove their own case
english: All heresies have now been challenged and refuted by these definitions. Let them dare to answer, whether they arose after the apostles or in their own time, so long as they were different; whether the apostles marked them out generally or specifically, so long as they were condemned beforehand. Let them dare to bring legal objections of this same kind against our discipline.

If they deny that our discipline is the truth, they must prove that it too is a heresy, refuted by the same form of argument by which they themselves are refuted. They must also show where the truth is to be sought, since it is already established that it is not among them.

Our teaching is not later than theirs. Indeed, it is prior to all of them, and this will be the testimony of the truth that everywhere holds first place. Everywhere the apostles do not condemn it; indeed, they defend it. This will be the proof of ownership. For the doctrine they do not condemn, after condemning every foreign one, they show to be their own, and therefore they defend it.
orientation: Tertullian has just shown that all heresies are late and already condemned; now he turns to the heretics and challenges them to answer with the same kind of legal objection against the church's discipline.

title: The apostolic churches as the living proof of the rule of faith
english: Come now, if you want to exercise your curiosity more profitably in the business of your salvation, travel through the apostolic churches, where the very chairs of the apostles still preside in their places, where their authentic letters are read aloud, sounding their voice and making each one's face present. Achaia is near you, so you have Corinth. If you are not far from Macedonia, you have Philippi and the Thessalonians. If you can make your way to Asia, you have Ephesus. If you are close to Italy, you have Rome, from which authority is also available to us.

How happy is that church, on which the apostles poured out their whole teaching with their own blood, where Peter is made equal to the Lord's passion, where Paul is crowned with John's departure, where the apostle John, after being cast into a cauldron of boiling oil and suffering nothing, is banished to an island. Let us see what he learned and what he taught, since he also entered into fellowship with the African churches. He acknowledges one God, the Lord, the creator of the universe, and Christ Jesus born of the virgin Mary, the Son of the creator God, and the resurrection of the flesh. He mingles the law and the prophets with the evangelical and apostolic writings; from these he drinks faith; he signs it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, urges it to martyrdom, and so he receives no one against this institution.

This is the institution—I do not say now the one that was foretelling future heresies, but the one from which heresies came forth. But they are not from it, since they were made against it. Even from the pit of the mild, rich, and necessary olive, the wild oleaster springs up; even from the poppy, the windy and empty wild fig rises from the most pleasing and sweet figs. So also heresies come from our shrub, but not of our kind—from the grain of truth, but wild with falsehood.
orientation: Tertullian is addressing a Christian who wants to exercise curiosity about salvation, telling him to visit the apostolic churches where the apostles' own chairs and authentic letters still remain.

title: The Church's inheritance and the heretics' exclusion
english: If this is how things stand, so that truth is adjudged to us who walk in that rule of faith which the church handed down from the apostles, the apostles from Christ, and Christ from God, then the reasoning of our position is established: we define that heretics must not be admitted to bring a challenge from the Scriptures, since we prove without the Scriptures that they have no claim to the Scriptures. For if they are heretics, they cannot be Christians, since they do not hold from Christ what they have followed by their own choice, and so they take on the name of heretics. Being therefore not Christians, they acquire no right to Christian writings, and to them it is rightly said: Who are you? When did you come, and from where? What are you doing on my property, you who are not mine? By what right, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? By what license, Valentinus, do you divert my springs? By what authority, Apelles, do you move my boundaries? The property is mine. Why do the rest of you sow and pasture here according to your own pleasure? The property is mine. I have possessed it from the beginning; I possessed it first. I hold firm origins from the very authors to whom the matter belonged. I am the heir of the apostles. As they provided in their testament, as they entrusted it to faith, as they bound it by oath, so I hold it. They certainly disinherited you always and renounced you as outsiders, as enemies. And why are heretics outsiders and enemies to the apostles, except because of the difference of doctrine, which each one by his own judgment either brought forward or received against the apostles?
orientation: Tertullian is speaking in his own voice, directly addressing heretics, claiming the apostolic inheritance of the Scriptures and denying heretics any right to them.

title: Corruption of doctrine and corruption of the instruments go together
english: Wherever you find diversity of doctrine, there you must locate the adulteration of both the Scriptures and their interpretations. Those who set out to teach differently were forced by necessity to arrange the instruments of doctrine differently. They could not have taught differently unless they had different instruments through which to teach. Just as the corruption of doctrine could not have succeeded for them without the corruption of its instruments, so the integrity of doctrine would not have been ours without the integrity of the instruments through which doctrine is handled.

For what is there in our own writings that is contrary to us? What have we introduced from our own resources, that we should need to remedy something contrary to us found in the Scriptures by removal or addition or alteration? What we are, the Scriptures are from their beginning. We are from them, before anything was different, before they were interpolated by you. But since every interpolation must be believed to be later, coming as it does from the cause of rivalry, which is never prior to or native to that which it rivals, it is as incredible to any wise person that we, who are from the beginning and first, should be thought to have introduced an adulterous pen to the Scriptures, as it is incredible that they did not introduce one, who are both later and opposed.

One person corrupts the Scriptures with his hand, another with his interpretation of their meaning. For even if Valentinus seems to use the document intact, he did not lay hands on the truth with less cunning talent than Marcion. Marcion used a sword openly and plainly, not a pen, since he carried out the slaughter of the Scriptures for his matter. Valentinus, however, spared them, since he did not devise the Scriptures for his matter, but his matter for the Scriptures, and yet he took away more and added more, removing the distinctive properties of each individual word and adding arrangements of things that do not exist.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretics have no right to use the Scriptures, and here he explains that doctrinal corruption necessarily involves corruption of the scriptural texts themselves.

title: The devil's counterfeits and the source of heresies
english: Such are the clever devices of the spiritual forces of wickedness with which we wrestle, brothers. They rightly deserve our attention, and they are necessary for faith, so that the elect may be made manifest and the reprobate may be uncovered. That is why they have power and facility in devising and constructing errors. This facility is not so remarkable, as if it were difficult and inexplicable, since an example of such facility is ready at hand even from secular writings. You see today how a story is composed from Virgil in a completely different way, with the subject matter fitted to the verses and the verses fitted to the subject matter. In fact, Hosidius Geta drew out a whole tragedy of Medea from Virgil. A relative of mine, among other leisure works of his pen, worked out the Tablet of Cebes from the same poet. People are even called Homer-centonists who stitch together into one body, in the manner of a patchwork, their own works from many passages of Homer's poems gathered here and there. And certainly the divine literature is more fertile for the capacity of any subject matter. Nor do I hesitate to say that the Scriptures themselves were arranged by God's will so that they might supply materials for heretics, since I read that there must be heresies, which cannot exist without the Scriptures.

It follows: by whom is the understanding of those things that make for heresies interpreted? By the devil, of course, whose part it is to pervert the truth, who also emulates the very realities of the divine sacraments in the mysteries of idols. He too baptizes certain people, his believers and faithful ones, of course. He promises the putting away of sins through the washing. And if I still remember, Mithras marks his soldiers there on their foreheads. He also celebrates an offering of bread, and introduces an image of the resurrection, and under the sword he buys back a crown. What of the fact that he also restricts his high priest to a single marriage? He has virgins too, and he has the continent. Moreover, if we review the superstitions of Numa Pompilius, if we consider the priestly offices and insignia and privileges, the sacrificial ministries and instruments and vessels of the sacrifices themselves, and the curiosities of expiations and vows, is it not clear that the devil imitated that scrupulosity of the Jewish law? Therefore he who so emulously desired to express the very realities by which the sacraments of Christ are administered in the business of idolatry, surely the same one, with the same talent, also desired and was able to adapt the instruments of divine realities and of holy Christians to a profane and rival faith: sense from senses, words from words, parables from parables. And therefore no one should doubt either that the spirits of wickedness, from which heresies also come, were sent by the devil, or that heresies differ from idolatry, since they are of the same author and the same work as idolatry. They either invent another god against the Creator, or if they confess the one Creator, they explain him differently than he is in truth. And so every falsehood they speak about God is in some way a kind of idolatry.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heresies were predicted and serve to test the faithful, and now explains that the devil, who counterfeits divine rites in idolatry, is the source of the spiritual wickedness from which heresies come.

title: The shameless disorder of heretical life
english: I will not pass over a description of the heretical way of life itself: how worthless it is, how earthly, how merely human, without seriousness, without authority, without discipline, as befits their faith. First of all, no one can tell who is a catechumen and who is a believer. They enter together, listen together, pray together, even pagans, if they happen to come in. They will throw the holy thing to dogs and pearls to pigs (Matthew 7:6), though the pearls are not genuine. They want simplicity to mean the overthrow of discipline, and they call our concern for discipline pandering. They also mix peace indiscriminately with everyone. It makes no difference to them, even though they hold different doctrines, as long as they conspire together to attack the one truth. They are all puffed up; they all promise knowledge. Their catechumens are complete before they are taught. And the heretical women, how shameless they are! They dare to teach, to argue, to perform exorcisms, to promise healings, perhaps even to baptize. Their ordinations are reckless, fickle, unstable. One day they appoint novices, the next day men bound to the world, the next day our apostates, so that they can bind them by honor since they cannot by truth. Nowhere is advancement easier than in the camp of rebels, where merely being there is a merit. So one man is bishop today and another tomorrow; today a deacon who tomorrow is a reader; today a presbyter who tomorrow is a layman. For they impose priestly duties even on laymen.

And what shall I say about their handling of the word, when their business is not converting pagans but overturning our own people? They seek this glory more: to bring ruin on those who stand, not to raise up those who lie fallen. Since their work does not come from building their own structure but from destroying the truth, they dig under ours to build their own. Take away from them the law of Moses, the prophets, and God the Creator, and they have no accusation left to speak. So it happens that they more easily reduce standing buildings to ruins than raise up what has fallen. Only for this work do they act humble, flattering, and submissive. Otherwise they show no reverence even for their own leaders. And this is why there are almost no schisms among heretics: because when schisms exist, they do not obey. For their very unity is a schism. I am lying if they do not also vary from their own rules among themselves, since each one arranges what he has received according to his own judgment, just as the one who handed it down composed it according to his own judgment. The development of the thing reveals its nature and the custom of its origin. The Valentinians were allowed the same thing as Valentinus, the Marcionites the same as Marcion: to innovate the faith according to their own judgment. In fact, when all heresies are thoroughly examined, they are found in many points disagreeing with their own founders. Most of them do not even have churches: without a mother, without a seat, destitute of faith, banished, they wander in their own worthlessness.
orientation: Tertullian has just argued that heresy is a kind of idolatry, and now he describes the conduct of heretics themselves to show that their way of life matches their false faith.

title: Heretics' character and the final judgment
english: Their dealings with a great many magicians, with wandering charlatans, with astrologers, with philosophers—all people devoted to curiosity—have also been noted. Everywhere they remember, “Seek and you will find” (Matthew 7:7). So the quality of their faith can be judged even from their way of life. Discipline is the index of doctrine. They deny that God must be feared. Therefore everything is free and unbound for them. But where is God not feared, except where He is not? Where God is not, there is no truth either. Where there is no truth, such discipline is deserved. But where God is, there is fear of God, which is the beginning of wisdom (Psalm 111:10). Where there is fear of God, there is seriousness, honest and attentive diligence, anxious care, tested recruitment, deliberate fellowship, mature promotion, religious submission, devout attendance, modest procession, a united church, and all things of God.

These stricter testimonies of discipline among us therefore support the proof of truth, from which it benefits no one to turn aside who remembers the future judgment, when we must all stand before the tribunal of Christ, giving an account first of all of faith itself (Romans 14:10). What then will they say who have defiled her with heretical adultery—the virgin handed over by Christ? I believe they will plead that nothing was ever foretold to them by Him or by His apostles about crooked and perverse doctrines to come, and no command given to avoid and abhor them. They will acknowledge instead their own fault and that of their own people, who did not fortify us beforehand. They will add many things about the authority of each heretical teacher: that those men especially confirmed faith in their doctrine, raised the dead, restored the weak, foretold the future, so that they were rightly believed to be apostles. As if this were not written: that many would come who would even perform the greatest wonders to strengthen the deception of corrupted preaching (Matthew 24:24). So they will deserve pardon.

But if they have stood in sound faith, remembering the Lord’s and the apostles’ writings and warnings, I believe they will be in danger of losing pardon, when the Lord answers: “I had clearly foretold that teachers of deception would come in My name, even in the name of the prophets and apostles, and I had commanded My disciples to preach the same things to you—since you would not believe. Once I had entrusted the gospel and the doctrine of the same rule to My apostles; later it pleased Me to change some things. I had promised the resurrection, even of the flesh; but I reconsidered, in case I could not fulfill it. I had shown Myself born of a virgin; but afterward it seemed shameful to Me. I had called the One who makes the sun and the rains Father; but another, better father adopted Me. I had forbidden you to lend your ear to heretics; but I was wrong.” Such are the things those people are forced to imagine who wander off course and do not guard against danger to the truth of faith.

For now, we have acted generally against all heresies, with certain, just, and necessary legal objections to keep them from any debate over the Scriptures. For the rest, if God’s grace permits, we will also answer certain ones specifically. To those who read these things in the faith of truth with leisure: peace and grace of our God Jesus Christ forever.
orientation: Tertullian is concluding his treatise by showing that the heretics' conduct reveals their false faith, then imagining their defense at the last judgment and answering it with the Lord's own words.
